description: HIBERNIA is a recovered inventory of historic buildings and streets in Dublin, combining two surveys by University College Dublin's School of Architecture, Landscape and Civil Engineering: the Dublin Environmental Inventory and the Dublin Docklands Area Master Plan inventory. The data were collected between 1993 and 1995, served from 2008 to 2013 through a searchable website, then recovered from digital and paper archives and deposited, with Debra Laefer as creator, in the UCD Digital Library, available from 18 August 2014. Each building record gives location, orthogonally corrected photographs for most buildings, and a detailed description of history, architecture and unique features with references; street records are similar but without images. Coverage: 1,280 buildings and 93 streets, plus over 800 further building records collected in the environmental inventory survey. Access: downloadable data files in buildings and streets collections on the UCD Digital Library. Licence: CC0; free. Caveats: a survey of the mid-1990s; many buildings may since have changed. Simulation uses: building characteristics and façade imagery for historic-building vulnerability, retrofit and heritage studies in Dublin. Related records: the Dublin Building Database (DUBLD).
